question: If you squeezed Earth's history into a single day, when would humans appear?
answer: In the last minute or so before midnight. Bryson uses the clock to show how recent we are: life appears early in the morning, complex animals only in the evening, dinosaurs late at night, and all of recorded history in the final few seconds.
move: On the scale of deep time, all of human history is seconds.
simply: If the Earth's whole life were one day, people would show up just before midnight, after the dinosaurs had come and gone.
why: Scaling huge numbers to a day is a tool worth borrowing for any vast quantity: it turns the unimaginable into something you can feel.
